metadata.title: Secure‑Resilience OT SSPP
metadata.remarks: System Security and Privacy Plan specializing Secure‑Resilience for Operational Technology (OT) environments where physical and process safety supersede availability and recovery speed.

import-profile.remarks: This SSPP inherits Secure‑Resilience Platform rules and applies OT‑specific safety and operational constraints.

system-characteristics.system-description: OT systems include industrial control systems, building automation, utilities, robotics, lab equipment, and safety‑critical cyber‑physical infrastructure. This SSPP enforces safe‑halt dominance, strict resume authorization, and conservative recovery to prevent physical harm or unsafe process states.

props.name: domain
props.remarks: Applies to OT systems controlling physical processes.

props.name: safety-authority
props.remarks: OT resilience is governed by IEC 62443 safety and security principles.

props.name: supporting-guidance
props.remarks: NIST guidance for securing and operating ICS environments.

props.name: state-assumption
props.remarks: OT system state is frequently irreversible due to physical outcomes.

props.name: preferred-resilience-outcome
props.remarks: Halt, isolate, or de‑energize is preferred over restore or resume.

props.name: implicit-restore
props.remarks: Backup restore or DR failover must not occur automatically.

props.name: implicit-resume
props.remarks: No OT system may resume operation without explicit safety authorization.

props.name: manual-override-preference
props.remarks: Manual or local control is preferred during resilience events.

system-implementation.remarks: OT resilience is implemented through strict application of Secure‑Resilience semantics with safety dominance. Recovery tooling is constrained to prevent unsafe physical actions.

components.title: OT Safety Overlay
components.remarks: Safety semantics from Secure‑Device override recovery actions.

components.title: Backup and Recovery
components.remarks: Backups are primarily forensic; restore is rare and tightly controlled.

components.title: Disaster Recovery
components.remarks: Alternate processing is limited and often excluded for OT systems.

components.title: Continuity of Operations
components.remarks: Continuity defaults to safe‑halt, manual operation, or isolation.

roles.title: OT Resilience Architecture
roles.remarks: Defines OT‑specific resilience and safety constraints.

roles.title: OT Resilience Governance
roles.remarks: Approves resume eligibility and safety authority decisions.

roles.title: OT Resilience Operations
roles.remarks: Executes halt, isolate, and controlled recovery actions under safety dominance.

roles.title: OT Resilience Monitoring
roles.remarks: Detects unsafe recovery attempts and physical risk escalation.

control-implementation.remarks: OT resilience is implemented through Secure‑Resilience constraints interpreted under IEC 62443 requirements and NIST SP 800‑53 CP controls. No new control requirements are introduced.
